examples.en: Above all, honesty is the most important thing for a politician.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 직원의 정직성을 가장 먼저 봐요.
examples.en: This company looks at an employee's integrity first.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 정직성은 누구도 의심하지 않아요.
examples.en: Nobody doubts that person's honesty.

examples.ko: 면접관이 정직성에 관한 질문을 자주 해요.
examples.en: Interviewers often ask questions about honesty.

examples.ko: 정직성 때문에 친구들이 그를 믿고 비밀을 말해요.
examples.en: Because of his honesty, his friends trust him and tell him their secrets.

examples.ko: 작은 거짓말 하나가 정직성까지 의심하게 만들어요.
examples.en: One small lie makes people doubt even your honesty.

explain: '정직'과 거의 같지만 '정직성'은 사람이나 조직이 가진 성질로 보고 평가하거나 따질 때 써요. '정직성이 높다', '정직성을 의심하다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '정직한 사람이에요'처럼 형용사로 말해도 돼요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '정직' (honesty), but '정직성' treats honesty as a quality of a person or organization that you evaluate or question. You say '정직성이 높다' or '정직성을 의심하다'. In daily talk you can also just say '정직한 사람이에요' with the adjective.

examples.en: At the start of the new year, families gather and do the New Year bow.
I had a rough time with a cold right from the start of the year.
Since it is the start of the year, shops close for a few days.
Next week is the start of the year. Are you going anywhere?
I plan to go down to my hometown during the New Year holiday.
The tteokguk you eat at the start of the year tastes the best.

explain: '연초'는 한 해의 처음 무렵을 넓게 말할 때 쓰고, '정초'는 설을 전후한 새해 첫머리 느낌이 더 강해요. '정초부터', '정초에는'처럼 새해 첫 며칠의 분위기를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: '연초' refers broadly to the early part of the year, while '정초' feels more like the very first days around the Lunar New Year. It fits phrases like '정초부터' and '정초에는' when you talk about the mood of those first days.

examples.en: He is closer to a political operator than a real statesman.

examples.ko: 표만 얻으려는 정치꾼은 믿을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You cannot trust a politician who only wants votes.
People call him a political schemer.
Whenever election season comes, political operators show up at the market.

examples.ko: 저는 말만 잘하는 정치꾼을 좋아하지 않아요.
examples.en: I do not like politicians who are only good at talking.
He answered like a slick politician, and I was disappointed.

explain: '정치인'이나 '정치가'는 중립적이거나 존중하는 말이지만 '정치꾼'은 이익과 요령만 챙기는 사람이라는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. '-꾼'은 '장사꾼', '일꾼'처럼 어떤 일을 하는 사람을 말하는데, 여기서는 부정적으로 쓰여요. 사람 앞에서 직접 말하면 무례해요.
explain_en: '정치인' and '정치가' are neutral or respectful, but '정치꾼' carries criticism, suggesting someone who only looks after their own interests and tricks. The '-꾼' ending appears in words like '장사꾼' and '일꾼' for people who do a certain job, but here it is negative. Saying it to someone's face is rude.

examples.ko: 요즘 정치판이 너무 시끄러워서 뉴스를 안 봐요.
examples.en: The political scene is so noisy these days that I do not watch the news.

examples.ko: 아버지는 정치판 이야기만 나오면 화를 내세요.
examples.en: My father gets angry whenever politics comes up.
He worked in politics for a long time.

examples.ko: 정치판은 말보다 힘이 센 곳이라고들 해요.
examples.en: People say the world of politics is a place where power counts more than words.

examples.ko: 저는 정치판에 뛰어들 생각이 전혀 없어요.
examples.en: I have no thought at all of jumping into politics.
Watching the fights in politics makes me frustrated.

explain: '정계'는 뉴스나 글에서 쓰는 중립적인 말이고, '정치판'은 정치 세계를 이익 다툼의 싸움터처럼 보며 말하는 구어예요. 그래서 '정치판이 시끄럽다', '정치판에 뛰어들다'처럼 약간 비꼬거나 못마땅한 기분이 담겨요. 중립적으로 말할 때는 '정치계'나 '정계'가 더 알맞아요.
explain_en: '정계' is a neutral word used in news and writing, while '정치판' is a spoken word that treats politics as an arena of fights over interests. So phrases like '정치판이 시끄럽다' and '정치판에 뛰어들다' carry a slightly sarcastic or disapproving tone. For a neutral tone, '정치계' or '정계' fits better.

examples.en: My child's baby tooth was loose, so we went to the dentist.

examples.ko: 젖니는 빠지고 나면 새 이가 나요.
examples.en: After a baby tooth falls out, a new tooth grows in.
My daughter had her first baby tooth pulled.
Baby teeth can get cavities too.

examples.ko: 젖니 때부터 양치하는 습관을 들여야 해요.
examples.en: You should build the habit of brushing from the baby-teeth stage.

examples.ko: 젖니에 구멍이 생기면 치과에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If a baby tooth gets a hole, you need to go to the dentist.

explain: 병원에서는 '유치'라고도 하고, 일상에서는 '젖니'라고 많이 말해요. 반대말은 평생 쓰는 '간니'(영구치)예요. 발음은 [전니]예요. 받침 'ㅈ'이 'ㄷ' 소리가 되고, 뒤의 'ㄴ' 때문에 다시 'ㄴ'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: At the dentist it is also called '유치', and in daily talk people say '젖니'. The opposite is '간니' (permanent tooth). It is pronounced [전니]: the final 'ㅈ' becomes a 'ㄷ' sound, and because of the following 'ㄴ' it then changes to 'ㄴ'.

examples.ko: 젖먹이를 안고 병원에 가는 엄마가 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw a mother carrying a nursing baby to the hospital.

examples.ko: 우리 집에는 젖먹이가 있어서 밤에 자주 깨요.
examples.en: We have a nursing baby at home, so I wake up often at night.

examples.ko: 젖먹이 때는 하루에도 몇 번씩 먹여야 해요.
examples.en: When they are nursing babies, you have to feed them several times a day.
Please dress the nursing baby in warm clothes.

examples.ko: 그 젖먹이도 이제 웃을 줄 알아요.
examples.en: That nursing baby can smile now too.

examples.ko: 동생이 젖먹이처럼 자꾸 안아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps asking to be held like a little baby.

explain: 아직 젖이나 분유를 먹는 시기의 아기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '아기'라고 말해도 되고, '젖먹이'는 이야기나 글에서 아주 어린 아기를 강조할 때 어울려요. 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아기는 '갓난아기'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a baby who is still drinking milk or formula. In daily talk you can just say '아기', and '젖먹이' fits stories or writing that stress how very young the baby is. A newborn is called '갓난아기'.

examples.ko: 아기가 젖병을 잡고 혼자 우유를 먹어요.
examples.en: The baby holds the bottle and drinks milk by himself.
Every night I mix formula in the bottle and feed the baby.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 젖병도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack the baby bottle when you travel.
I needed a new baby bottle, so I went to the mart.

examples.ko: 아기 젖병은 끓는 물 소독이 필요해요.
examples.en: Baby bottles need to be sterilized in boiling water.

examples.ko: 젖병 꼭지가 너무 커서 아기가 힘들어해요.
examples.en: The bottle nipple is too big, so the baby has a hard time.

explain: 아기에게 우유나 분유를 먹이는 병이에요. '젖병을 물리다'는 아기에게 젖병을 입에 물려 먹인다는 말이고, '젖병을 떼다'는 아기가 젖병 쓰는 것을 끝낸다는 말이에요. 병의 끝에 붙은 부분은 '젖꼭지'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the bottle used to feed a baby milk or formula. '젖병을 물리다' means to put the bottle in the baby's mouth to feed, and '젖병을 떼다' means the baby stops using bottles. The nipple part on the bottle is called '젖꼭지'.

examples.ko: 이제 두 달 된 아기는 얼굴에 젖살이 포동포동해요.
examples.en: The two-month-old baby has plump baby fat on her face.

examples.ko: 조카는 젖살을 빼고 나니 훨씬 의젓해 보여요.
examples.en: After losing her baby fat, my niece looks much more mature.
As children grow, their baby fat also slowly goes away.

examples.ko: 젖살은 네 살쯤 되니까 거의 사라졌어요.
examples.en: The baby fat almost disappeared when he was about four.

examples.ko: 젖살 때문에 볼이 터질 것 같아요.
examples.en: Her cheeks look like they will burst because of the baby fat.
Your cheeks are still soft like baby fat.

explain: 아기 때 얼굴이나 몸에 통통하게 붙어 있는 살이에요. 어른이나 큰 아이에게 '젖살이 안 빠졌다'고 하면 얼굴이 아직 어려 보이고 통통하다는 말인데, 놀리는 느낌이 될 수도 있어요. '볼살'은 볼에 있는 살이라서 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It is the plump flesh a baby has on the face and body. Saying an older child or adult 'hasn't lost the 젖살' means their face still looks young and chubby, which can sound like teasing. '볼살' just means the flesh of the cheeks, so it is used differently.

examples.ko: 공사 현장 일꾼은 숙식을 제공받아서 월급을 거의 모았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the construction workers got room and board, so they saved almost all their pay.
I get lunch provided by my company.
I was provided with a laptop by my school.

examples.ko: 이 앱으로 실시간 교통 정보를 제공받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this app you can receive real-time traffic information.

examples.ko: 무료로 제공받은 쿠폰은 이번 달까지 써야 해요.
examples.en: The coupon I got for free has to be used by the end of this month.

examples.ko: 서비스를 제공받으려면 먼저 회원 가입을 하세요.
examples.en: To receive the service, please sign up as a member first.

explain: 주는 쪽은 '제공하다', 받는 쪽은 '제공받다'예요. '회사에서 숙소를 제공받다'처럼 '-에서/-에게 ~을 제공받다'로 써요. 말할 때는 '(무료로) 받다'로 바꿔도 되지만 '제공받다'가 공식적인 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '제공하다' is for the giver and '제공받다' is for the receiver. Use it like '회사에서 숙소를 제공받다', with -에서/-에게 marking the source. In casual speech you can say '(무료로) 받다' instead, but '제공받다' sounds more formal.

examples.en: On Seollal we play jegichagi with the family.
How many kicks have you managed in jegichagi?

examples.ko: 제기차기 대회에서 우리 반이 일등 했어요.
examples.en: Our class won first place in the jegichagi contest.

examples.ko: 제기차기도 해 보고 윷놀이도 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried jegichagi and yutnori too.

examples.ko: 제기차기에 도전했는데 한 번도 못 찼어요.
examples.en: I tried jegichagi but could not kick it even once.
Kite flying, jegichagi and neolttwigi are Korean folk games.

explain: 놀이에 쓰는 물건 이름이 '제기'라서 '제기를 차다'라고도 말해요. 제사 때 쓰는 그릇인 '제기(祭器)'와 소리는 같지만 다른 말이에요. 설날 무렵 윷놀이, 연날리기 같은 민속놀이와 함께 많이 이야기해요.
explain_en: The object used in the game is called a '제기', so you can also say '제기를 차다'. It sounds the same as '제기(祭器)', the vessels used for ancestral rites, but it is a different word. People often talk about it around Seollal together with folk games like yutnori and kite flying.

examples.en: In summer, cold noodles are at their best.
Kimchi only gets its true taste once it is well fermented.

examples.ko: 이 집 떡볶이는 매워야 제맛을 느낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only get the real flavor of this place's tteokbokki when it is spicy.

examples.ko: 땀 흘린 뒤에 마시는 물이 제맛인 걸 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know that water tastes best after you sweat?

examples.ko: 제맛은 역시 직접 담근 김치에서 나와요.
examples.en: The real flavor comes from kimchi you made yourself.
Isn't this exactly the real thing?

explain: 'N이 제맛이다'는 어떤 음식이나 일이 가장 좋을 때, 또는 그렇게 해야 진짜 맛이 난다고 말하는 표현이에요. 음식뿐 아니라 '운동은 새벽에 해야 제맛이다'처럼 즐거움에도 써요. 발음은 [제맏]이에요.
explain_en: 'N이 제맛이다' says that something is at its best or that you only get the real enjoyment in that way. It is not only for food; you can say '운동은 새벽에 해야 제맛이다' for other pleasures too. It is pronounced [제맏].

examples.en: My younger sister got married, so I now have a brother-in-law.

examples.ko: 제부도 우리 가족 모임에 올 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard my sister's husband can come to our family gathering too.
On the weekend I went fishing with my sister's husband.
Yesterday I got a birthday present from my sister's husband.
I asked my sister's husband to look after the child.

examples.ko: 동생과 제부는 서울에 살고 저는 부산에 살아요.
examples.en: My sister and her husband live in Seoul and I live in Busan.

explain: 여자가 여동생의 남편을 부르거나 가리키는 말이에요. 남자가 누이동생의 남편을 말할 때는 '매제'라고 하고, 언니의 남편은 '형부'라고 해요. 가족 호칭은 말하는 사람의 성별에 따라 달라져서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: A woman uses it for her younger sister's husband. A man calls his younger sister's husband '매제', and a woman calls her older sister's husband '형부'. Family terms change depending on the speaker's gender, so they are easy to mix up.

examples.en: When spring comes, violets bloom along the road.
While taking a walk, I found a violet by the roadside.
My mother likes handkerchiefs with a violet pattern.
Violets are small but smell nice.
The children played making rings out of violets.
Shall we plant some violets in the pot too?

explain: 봄에 길가나 풀밭에서 볼 수 있는 작은 꽃이에요. 보라색을 많이 떠올리지만 '노랑제비꽃', '흰제비꽃'처럼 다른 색도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a small flower you can see along roads and in meadows in spring. People often picture purple, but there are other colors too, like '노랑제비꽃' (yellow) and '흰제비꽃' (white).

examples.en: My mother is preparing the food to put on the ancestral rites table.

examples.ko: 제사상이 너무 커서 상을 두 개 붙였어요.
examples.en: The ritual table was so big that we put two tables together.

examples.ko: 제사상은 집안마다 차리는 방법이 조금씩 달라요.
examples.en: How the ritual table is set differs a little from family to family.

examples.ko: 큰집에서 제사상을 차리고 모두 절을 했어요.
examples.en: At my uncle's house we set the ritual table and everyone bowed.
In front of the ritual table, the family members bow one by one.

examples.ko: 제사상까지 다 차리고 나니 밤이 되었어요.
examples.en: By the time we finished setting even the ritual table, it was night.

explain: 조상에게 제사를 지낼 때 음식을 차려 놓는 상이에요. '상을 차리다'처럼 '제사상을 차리다'라고 말해요. 설이나 추석 아침에 지내는 제사는 '차례'라고 해서 일반 '제사'와 구분하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the table where food is laid out when holding rites for ancestors. You say '제사상을 차리다', like '상을 차리다'. The rites held on the morning of Seollal or Chuseok are called '차례', which is sometimes distinguished from a regular '제사'.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 집 안이 습하니까 제습기를 켜 놓아요.
examples.en: During the rainy season the house is damp, so I leave the dehumidifier on.
The dehumidifier's water tank was full, so I emptied it.
The dehumidifier broke, so I called the service center.
I tried getting rid of the moisture in the closet with a dehumidifier.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 에어컨뿐 아니라 제습기도 필요해요.
examples.en: Our home needs a dehumidifier, not just an air conditioner.

examples.ko: 제습기는 밤에 켜 두면 소리가 좀 커요.
examples.en: If you leave the dehumidifier on at night, it is a bit loud.

explain: 공기 속 습기를 없애는 기계예요. 반대로 습기를 더하는 기계는 '가습기'라서 소리가 비슷해 헷갈릴 수 있어요. 에어컨에도 '제습 모드'가 있어서 따로 제습기를 쓰지 않는 집도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a machine that removes moisture from the air. The opposite, a machine that adds moisture, is a '가습기', and the two sound alike, so they are easy to mix up. Air conditioners also have a '제습 모드' (dry mode), so some homes do not use a separate dehumidifier.

examples.en: Be sure to check the production date when you buy milk.
This snack was made yesterday.
The production date and the sell-by date are written together.
Where is the production date on the package?
Please eat it within a year of the production date.

examples.ko: 제조일 확인 없이 사면 후회할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you buy without checking the production date, you may regret it.

explain: 물건을 만든 날짜예요. 팔 수 있는 기한인 '유통기한', 먹어도 되는 기한인 '소비기한'과 달라서 제품에 같이 적혀 있기도 해요. 같은 뜻으로 '제조일자'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the date a product was made. It differs from '유통기한' (the date until which it can be sold) and '소비기한' (the date until which it can be eaten), and these may all be printed on the same product. '제조일자' means the same thing.

examples.en: I was angry and tore the paper to pieces.
I cut the cake into pieces and shared it with my friends.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 조각내는 바람에 고칠 수 없어요.
examples.en: The child broke the toy to pieces, so it cannot be fixed.
After reading the letter, he tore it to pieces.
I took out a knife to cut the cookie into pieces.

examples.ko: 빵을 조각내지 말고 통째로 구워 주세요.
examples.en: Please bake the bread whole without cutting it into pieces.

explain: '조각나다'는 저절로 조각이 되는 것이고, '조각내다'는 누가 일부러 또는 실수로 조각을 만드는 것이에요. '깨다', '자르다'보다 결과가 여러 조각이라는 점을 강조해요. 목적어를 꼭 같이 써서 '무엇을 조각내다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '조각나다' means something breaks into pieces by itself, while '조각내다' means someone makes pieces, on purpose or by accident. Compared with '깨다' or '자르다', it stresses that the result is several pieces. It takes an object: '무엇을 조각내다'.

examples.en: I have a habit of reading the morning paper every morning.
The morning paper is delivered to the front of the house at dawn.

examples.ko: 아버지는 조간신문에 난 기사를 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father showed me an article in the morning paper.

examples.ko: 요즘은 조간신문 대신 휴대폰으로 뉴스를 봐요.
examples.en: These days I read the news on my phone instead of the morning paper.
The morning paper is lying at the door.
Morning papers and evening papers come out at different times.

explain: 아침에 나오는 신문이에요. 저녁에 나오는 신문은 '석간신문'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 요즘은 종이신문 대신 인터넷으로 보는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: It is a newspaper that comes out in the morning. The evening paper is '석간신문', so it is good to learn them as a pair. These days many people read news online instead of on paper.

examples.en: I picked up a pretty seashell at the beach.
The child made a necklace out of shells.

examples.ko: 모래 속에 조개껍질이 많이 묻혀 있어요.
examples.en: Lots of shells are buried in the sand.

examples.ko: 조개껍질은 버리지 말고 따로 모아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't throw the shells away; collect them separately.

examples.ko: 조개껍질 안에 작은 게가 숨어 있었어요.
examples.en: A small crab was hiding inside the shell.

examples.ko: 책상 위에는 여행에서 가져온 조개껍질도 있어요.
examples.en: There are shells I brought back from a trip on the desk too.

explain: '조개껍데기'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 표준어예요. '껍질'은 과일 껍질처럼 얇은 겉을, '껍데기'는 조개나 달걀처럼 단단한 겉을 말할 때 쓰는 편이에요. 바닷가에서 주운 것이나 기념품을 말할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '조개껍데기' is a standard word with the same meaning. '껍질' tends to be used for a thin outer layer like fruit skin, and '껍데기' for a hard outer layer like a clam or egg. It comes up often when talking about shells picked up at the beach or souvenirs.

examples.ko: 조리대 위에 칼과 도마를 올려 두었어요.
examples.en: I put the knife and cutting board on the counter.
The counter is narrow, so cooking is inconvenient.
When I finish cooking, I wipe the counter clean.

examples.ko: 조리대는 늘 정리해 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is best to keep the counter tidy at all times.
I lined the vegetables up on the counter.
The space between the counter and the sink is too narrow.

explain: 음식을 썰고 만드는 작업 공간이에요. '싱크대'는 설거지하는 쪽을 말할 때가 많아서 '조리대'와 구분해서 쓰기도 해요. 집에서는 '싱크대 옆 작업대'처럼 풀어서 말해도 돼요.
explain_en: It is the work surface where you cut and prepare food. '싱크대' often refers to the washing side, so people sometimes separate it from '조리대'. At home you can also just say something like '싱크대 옆 작업대'.

examples.en: I bought a bookshelf kit and put it together myself.

examples.ko: 이 침대는 조립식이라서 이사할 때 편해요.
examples.en: This bed is the assembly type, so it is convenient when moving.

examples.ko: 방을 조립식으로 만들면 빨리 지을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you build the room as a prefab, you can finish it quickly.
I bought it without knowing it was self-assembly and had a hard time.

examples.ko: 조립식은 값이 싸지만 튼튼하지 않을 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Assembly-type items are cheap but sometimes not sturdy.
These days even self-assembly furniture has pretty designs.

explain: 부품을 사서 직접 맞춰 만드는 방식을 말해서 '조립식 가구', '조립식 주택'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요. 반대로 이미 다 만들어진 상태로 파는 것은 '완제품'이라고 해요. '조립식이다'처럼 서술어로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes things you put together from parts, and it modifies a noun that follows, as in '조립식 가구' or '조립식 주택'. The opposite, something sold already assembled, is a '완제품'. You can also use it as a predicate: '조립식이다'.

examples.ko: 통계청 조사원이 집을 방문해서 가구 구성과 소득을 물어봤어요.
examples.en: A Statistics Office surveyor visited my home and asked about household members and income.
The surveyor showed his ID first.

examples.ko: 저는 인구 조사원으로 일한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once worked as a census surveyor.
Please answer the surveyor's questions honestly.
I saw a notice recruiting surveyors on the internet.
Surveyors go around the village asking for people's opinions.

explain: 설문이나 통계를 위해 사람들을 만나 물어보고 기록하는 사람이에요. '조사관'은 사건이나 위반을 조사하는 공무원에게 써서 느낌이 달라요. 보통 '인구 조사원', '여론 조사원'처럼 앞에 조사 종류를 붙여요.
explain_en: It is a person who meets people to ask questions and record answers for surveys or statistics. '조사관' is used for officials who investigate cases or violations, so it feels different. People usually put the kind of survey in front, like '인구 조사원' or '여론 조사원'.

examples.ko: 아이는 들고 있던 조약돌을 멀리 던졌어요.
examples.en: The child threw the pebble he was holding far away.
Round pebbles are spread along the stream.
Pebbles are smooth because water has washed them for a long time.
I put one pebble in my pocket and came back.
You have a round face like a pebble on the beach.
I made a path with pebbles in the garden.

explain: 냇가나 바닷가에서 볼 수 있는 작고 동글동글한 돌이에요. '자갈'은 여러 개가 깔려 있는 작은 돌을 말할 때가 많고, '조약돌'은 매끈하고 둥근 모양이 먼저 떠올라요. 아이들이 줍거나 던지고 노는 장면에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a small round stone you find by streams and beaches. '자갈' often refers to many small stones spread out, while '조약돌' brings to mind the smooth, round shape. It often appears in scenes of children picking up or throwing stones.

examples.en: The cockpit door on an airplane is locked.
The captain made an announcement from the cockpit.
The child said he wanted to look at the cockpit.
The inside of the cockpit was full of instrument panels.
The spaceship cockpit looked cool in the movie.

examples.ko: 조종실은 승객이 마음대로 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Passengers cannot enter the cockpit freely.

explain: 비행기나 배, 우주선을 조종하는 사람이 있는 방이에요. 자동차는 '운전석'이라고 하고, 승객이 앉는 곳은 '객실'이라고 해서 구분해요. 외래어 '콕핏'은 비행기나 레이싱에서 쓰는 경우가 있어요.
explain_en: It is the room where the person who operates a plane, ship or spaceship sits. For cars you say '운전석', and the place where passengers sit is the '객실'. The loanword '콕핏' is sometimes used for planes or racing.

en: leave work early; leave school early

examples.ko: 저 오늘 볼일이 좀 있는데, 지금 조퇴하면 안 될까요?
examples.en: I have something to take care of today. Could I leave early now?
I caught the flu and left school early after first period.
If you do not feel well, it is fine to leave early.

examples.ko: 내일은 병원 예약 때문에 조퇴하려고 해요.
examples.en: Tomorrow I plan to leave early because of a hospital appointment.
I felt awkward at work, so I could not leave early.

examples.ko: 아이가 아프다고 해서 일찍 조퇴해야 했어요.
examples.en: My child said he was sick, so I had to leave early.

explain: 학교나 회사에서 정해진 시간보다 일찍 나오는 것을 말해요. 반대로 늦게 오면 '지각', 하루 종일 안 가면 '결석'이라고 해요. 회사에서는 '반차'를 써서 반나절을 쉬기도 해요.
explain_en: It means leaving school or work earlier than scheduled. Arriving late is '지각', and missing the whole day is '결석'. At work people sometimes use '반차' to take half a day off.

examples.en: I tidied my eyebrows with tweezers while looking in the mirror.
A thorn got stuck in my hand, so I looked for tweezers.
You need tweezers to pull out a thorn.
I took cram tutoring before the exam.
The tweezers are in the medicine box.

examples.ko: 족집게에 끼운 털이 잘 안 빠져요.
examples.en: The hair caught in the tweezers will not come out easily.

explain: 털이나 가시처럼 작은 것을 집어 뽑는 도구예요. '핀셋'도 비슷한 도구인데 '핀셋'은 실험, 의료, 공예 같은 정밀한 작업에서 더 자주 떠올라요. 도구 이름에서 나온 비유로 정확히 집어내는 사람이나 선생님을 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 선생님은 시험에 나올 문제를 족집게처럼 맞히세요.
phrases.en: That teacher predicts the exam questions with uncanny accuracy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 가시를 쏙 뽑는 도구처럼, 딱 집어서 정확히 알아맞힌다는 뜻이에요. 정확한 예측에 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a tool that plucks out a tiny thorn, it means picking out exactly the right thing. Used to admire very accurate guesses or predictions.

phrases.en: I took cram tutoring that targets likely questions before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에 나올 만한 내용만 콕 집어 가르쳐 주는 과외나 강의예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tutoring or a class that picks out only what is likely to appear on the exam.

explain_en: It is a tool for gripping and pulling small things like hairs or thorns. '핀셋' is a similar tool, but it brings to mind precision work such as experiments, medicine or crafts. By extension, it is also used figuratively for people or teachers who pick out the right thing exactly.

examples.ko: 나이가 어린 사람에게도 존대하는 분이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people use polite speech even to younger people.
We have just met, so we speak politely to each other.
My mother always speaks politely even to those younger than her.
We are friends, so it feels awkward when you suddenly speak formally.
The mood changed when you started speaking politely.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 어른께 존대하지 않는다고 야단을 맞았어요.
examples.en: As a child I got scolded for not speaking politely to adults.

explain: 상대를 높여서 말하거나 대한다는 뜻으로, 특히 말투를 높이는 상황에서 많이 나와요. 반대는 '하대하다'이고, 일상에서는 '존댓말을 쓰다', '말을 높이다'라고 해도 자연스러워요. 반말과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It means to treat or speak to someone with respect, and it comes up especially when talking about raising your speech level. The opposite is '하대하다', and in daily talk '존댓말을 쓰다' or '말을 높이다' also sound natural. It helps to remember it as a pair with '반말'.
